sections.overview: Hampala macrolepidota is a large Southeast Asian cyprinid of the Mekong, Chao Phraya, Malay Peninsula, and Indonesian freshwaters.
sections.identification: Adults show a dark flank bar and black-edged orange-red tail; reported maximum standard length is 70 cm, versus a common 35 cm.
sections.habitat: It inhabits flowing rivers and streams with clear water and sandy or muddy bottoms, and also enters flooded forest and larger water bodies.
sections.diet: It is predatory, but the balance between fish and insect prey varies by locality; aquatic insects can dominate some reservoir samples.
sections.behavior: The species is potamodromous, moving within freshwater systems, and enters flooded forest habitats.
sections.reproduction: FishBase reports breeding through the rainy season, but no single spawning date or detailed clutch figure is established here.
sections.ecology: Its opportunistic predation links riverine and floodplain food webs, while local diet studies show that prey availability changes its feeding profile.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports Least Concern in the IUCN assessment dated 2019; the species is also taken in commercial and recreational fisheries.
